conflict_topics: seat reservation norm (tissue packet) vs current occupant's right to remain
hot food urgency (A) vs risk of spilling an open bowl (B)
third party (D) waiting to take seat when free
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete practical reasons (hot food, spill risk), which grounds the dispute in real trade-offs.
Several rounds repeat the same short exchanges ('I'm sitting now', 'I'll wait until it's genuinely free'), producing moderate redundancy.
Agent D's stance shifts from potential claimant to conditional waiter, which is clearly signaled in successive turns.
evaluation.final_reason: The main incompatibility between Agent A (demanding to sit now, citing a tissue packet reservation and hot food) and Agent B (refusing to move because an open bowl would spill and stating they will finish and then give the seat) was never affirmatively settled. Key lines: Turn 1 (A) 'That's my seat — I left the tissue packet... please move so I can sit.' Turn 2 (B) '...I'm still eating and that bowl will spill if I carry it. I'll finish here and then you can have the seat.' Although Agent D ultimately agrees to wait (e.g. Turn 21, Turn 25), Agent B never consents to A sitting immediately and no mutual, concrete spoken agreement resolving A vs B appears in the transcript; therefore the conflict remains unresolved.
position_change_notes: Agent B retained their original position throughout: refused to move until finished (Turn 2, Turn 7); no concession permitting A to sit immediately is recorded.
Agent A repeatedly asserted an immediate claim and later stated they were sitting (Turn 1, Turn 3, Turn 6, Turn 12, Turn 15, Turn 17) but B never acknowledged that as acceptable.

Agent D softened their stance over time: initially said they'd take the seat when free (Turn 9), then clarified conditionality (Turn 11), and ultimately agreed to wait until the seat was 'actually free' (Turns 16, 21, 25).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 (Agent A): 'That's my seat — I left the tissue packet to reserve it. ... please move so I can sit.' vs Turn 2 (Agent B): 'I moved the tissue packet but I didn't mean to take your spot. I'm still eating and that bowl will spill if I carry it. I'll finish here and then you can have the seat.' — clear, substantive disagreement about who should occupy the seat now.

Turn 3 (Agent A) reiterates demand and urgency: 'Put the tissue packet back on the seat so I can sit now... I need the seat as soon as you're done.' Turn 5 (Agent D) corroborates A's earlier placement of the packet. The substantive dispute (A wants seat now; B refuses until finished) persists without settlement.

Turn 6 (Agent A) presses again: 'Put it back and let me sit now—my food's hot.' Turn 7 (Agent B) repeats refusal based on practical risk: 'I can't carry this open bowl; it'll spill. I'll finish here and you can have the seat right after.' No agreement reached.

Turn 9 (Agent D): 'I'll take that seat as soon as it's genuinely free.' Turn 10 (Agent A): 'Agent D — don't take that seat. I left the tissue packet to reserve it; I'm sitting now.' The dispute expands (A vs B and now contested by D), increasing substantive tension over entitlement and timing.

Turn 11 (Agent D): 'I'm only taking it when it's genuinely free... otherwise I'll sit as soon as Agent B finishes.' Turn 12 (Agent A): 'Agent D — I'm sitting now. Don't take the seat.' Multiple claims persist and no party whose demand was in conflict accepts the other's arrangement.

Turn 15 (Agent A): repeats 'I'm sitting here now.' Turn 16 (Agent D): softens: 'If you're actually sitting, it's not free — I'll wait until it's genuinely free.' D's conditional withdrawal reduces the number of active claimants, but the core A vs B incompatibility remains (B still occupying/using seat).

Turn 17 (Agent A): 'Okay — I'm sitting now.' Turn 21 (Agent D): 'Alright — I'll wait until it's genuinely free.' D accepts waiting, but B has not agreed to A's claimed immediate occupation and earlier stated they will remain until finished, so substantive conflict is unresolved.

Turn 25 (Agent D): 'Okay — I'll wait here until that seat's actually free.' D continues to wait. No statement from Agent B conceding that A may sit now or that B will leave immediately; the central incompatible practical state (seat occupied by B vs A's demand to sit now) persists.

substantive_insights: A's claim rests on a social reservation signal (tissue packet) and urgency (hot food); B's refusal is grounded in a safety/practical constraint (open bowl risk).
D's willingness to wait reduces multi-party competition but does not resolve the core incompatible physical state (B occupying the seat vs A's demand to sit now).
No party provided or accepted a concrete, mutual arrangement (who moves when, or who actually vacates/takes a seat), so the disagreement could not be declared settled from speech alone.
